_meta.indication: Topical treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in patients 2 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, vehicle-controlled trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to EUCRISA or vehicle applied twice daily for 28 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects aged 2 years and older with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, BSA ≥ 5%, and ISGA score of 2 (mild) or 3 (moderate).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects at Day 29 achieving success, defined as an ISGA grade of Clear (0) or Almost Clear (1) with a 2-grade or greater improvement from baseline.
pivotal_trials.n: Trial 301 randomized 763 subjects (507 to EUCRISA and 256 to vehicle); 4 of the 507 EUCRISA subjects were not dispensed study drug, leaving an EUCRISA ITT N of 503.
pivotal_trials.result: Success in ISGA at Day 29: EUCRISA 32.8% vs vehicle 25.4%; P-value 0.038.

key_safety: The most common adverse reaction (≥1%) was application site pain, reported in 45 (4%) of EUCRISA-treated subjects vs 6 (1%) of vehicle. Less common (<1%) adverse reactions included contact urticaria.
target_moa: Crisaborole is a phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE-4) inhibitor; PDE-4 inhibition results in increased intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) levels.
modality: Small molecule (topical boron-containing PDE-4 inhibitor ointment, 2%).

rems.type: Based on the favorable safety profile of this topical drug product, risk mitigation measures beyond professional labeling are not warranted; no REMS required.

advisory_committee.vote: The Agency conducted no Advisory Committee Meeting regarding this application.

basis.text: The applicant requested priority review, but the Division did not grant it; the review classification was standard because atopic dermatitis is not a serious condition (no increased mortality or permanent disability).

citations.quote: The applicant included a Request for Priority Review Designation in the NDA submission. The Division did not grant the priority review request because although atopic dermatitis (AD) may be a severe condition, it is not a serious condition since it does not result in increased mortality or permanent disability. summary.text: EUCRISA was reviewed as a standard NDA (application received 01/07/2016, PDUFA goal date 01/06/2017); the applicant's priority review request was denied and no advisory committee was convened. Approval was based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 vehicle-controlled trials (AN2728-AD-301 and AN2728-AD-302), with a deferred pediatric study required under PREA as a postmarketing requirement.
